content: For young individuals with Type 1 Diabetes who exhibit abnormal lipid profiles, the primary approach to management involves the optimization of dietary habits and engagement in regular physical activity. If low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol levels remain persistently elevated at or above 130 mg/dL (≥3.4 mmol/L), the initiation of statin therapy should be considered once the patient reaches the age of 10 years. This pharmacological intervention should be implemented in conjunction with continued lifestyle modifications. For individuals whose LDL cholesterol levels are below 100 mg/dL (2.6 mmol/L), the use of statin therapy is generally not deemed necessary.
